text: Patient presents with worsening dyspnea on exertion over 2 weeks. Bilateral ankle edema. BNP elevated at 1200 pg/mL. Echo shows EF 30%.
Routine cholesterol recheck. Total cholesterol 195, LDL 110, HDL 55, triglycerides 150. Statin well tolerated. Continue same dose.
Acute kidney injury with creatinine rising from 1.0 to 4.5 over 48 hours. Oliguria. Potassium 6.2. Metabolic acidosis pH 7.25. Nephrology consulted.
Well-child visit 3-year-old. Height and weight at 60th percentile. Speech development normal. Social skills age-appropriate. No parental concerns.
New-onset status epilepticus in pregnancy at 32 weeks. No prior seizure history. Eclampsia suspected. Magnesium loading. Fetal monitoring initiated.
Patient seen for annual flu shot. No contraindications. Vaccine administered left deltoid. Observed for 15 minutes. No adverse reaction. Released.
Bilateral pneumothoraces after central line placement attempt. Respiratory distress SpO2 82%. Bilateral chest tubes inserted emergently. CXR post-procedure improved.
Follow-up for well-controlled hypothyroidism. TSH 2.1 within target range. Patient asymptomatic. Continue levothyroxine same dose. Recheck in 6 months.
Massive hemoptysis estimated 500mL in 2 hours. Patient on anticoagulation for mechanical valve. INR 4.5. Intubation for airway protection. Reversed with PCC.
Routine skin cancer screening for patient with history of sun exposure. Full body exam performed. No suspicious lesions identified. Annual follow-up recommended.
Acute inferior STEMI with complete heart block. Ventricular rate 35. Temporary pacing wire placed. Emergent PCI of RCA performed with drug-eluting stent.
Pre-operative clearance for cataract surgery. ASA class I. No cardiac risk factors. Labs normal. ECG normal. Cleared for local anesthesia procedure.
Addisonian crisis presenting with shock after abrupt corticosteroid cessation. Random cortisol 1.2 mcg/dL. Stress-dose hydrocortisone and aggressive resuscitation initiated.
Lactation consultation for new mother. Latch technique reviewed and corrected. Infant gaining weight appropriately. Supportive counseling provided. Follow up in 1 week.
Acute promyelocytic leukemia with DIC. Platelets 12K, fibrinogen 80, D-dimer markedly elevated. ATRA started emergently. Cryoprecipitate and platelets transfusing.
Annual Medicare wellness visit. Advance directive reviewed. Fall risk assessment negative. Cognitive screening normal. Depression screening negative. Immunizations current.
Pheochromocytoma crisis during surgery. BP 280/160, HR 180. Phentolamine IV bolus given. Esmolol drip for rate control. Surgery temporarily halted.
Routine prenatal visit 20 weeks. Anatomy scan normal. Fetal movements felt. Blood pressure 108/68. No edema or proteinuria. Uneventful pregnancy.
Massive retroperitoneal hemorrhage post renal biopsy. Dropping hemoglobin from 12 to 6 in 3 hours. CT confirms active extravasation. IR embolization planned.
Patient presents for travel vaccines before trip to Africa. Yellow fever and typhoid vaccines administered. Malaria prophylaxis prescribed. Travel advice provided.
Ludwig's angina with floor of mouth swelling and airway compromise. Stridor present. Awake fiberoptic intubation performed. IV antibiotics and surgical drainage.
Routine diabetic foot exam. Monofilament testing intact all sites. Pedal pulses 2+ bilateral. No calluses ulcers or deformities. Good foot hygiene.
Acute transfusion reaction. Fever rigors back pain dark urine 15 minutes into pRBC transfusion. Transfusion stopped immediately. DIC labs sent. Supportive care.
Weight management follow-up. Patient lost 5 lbs since last visit. Adherent to dietary plan. Increasing exercise frequency. Encouraged to continue progress.
Flail chest with respiratory failure after crush injury. Multiple rib fractures bilaterally. Pulmonary contusions. Intubated for ventilatory support. CT chest performed.
